entry_state: Actual and hypothetical options retain separate payoffs and component values; a matched collar can carry signed reserves despite zero initial net premium. Rebalancing preserves cumulative gains and each item or instrument designation origin. Added derivative carrying value includes acquisition cost, which is not a hedge gain. Instrument reduction has begun: the removed fraction retains earlier gains but its subsequent changes enter earnings; the general history formulas continue next.
exit_state: Instrument reductions retain earlier gains and measure later undesignated changes separately. A stopped purchase portion carries its own frozen reserve, whose later release depends on expectation and recoverability. Distinct designation origins cannot be allocated by nominal quantity alone. The inventory transfer now separates basis, cash and profit; the warning that equal final totals can hide wrong interim accounting continues next.
findings: The stopped-instrument history reconciles designated and undesignated gains without removing purchase units.
Homogeneous partial discontinuation is derived separately from the restricted origin-matched case; neither is promoted to a general heterogeneous allocation rule.
The origin examples preserve gross supplier and derivative cash, funding order, named stopped reserves and prior loss releases.
The inventory example begins a useful counterexample: final profit agreement cannot establish correct interim inventory or profit. No new confirmed defect.
